subject: Post-demo: security questionnaire, in-scope systems & decision roster
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Zhang <evelyn.zhang@orchidhealth.com>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: security questionnaire, in-scope systems & decision roster

Hi Evelyn / Tom —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from Redwood on the asks and the next steps we discussed so we’re aligned on scope and owners: 

- Immediate asks from Orchid: a completed security questionnaire and clarification of which systems will be in scope for the review (EHR, scheduling integration, analytics, etc.).
- Suggested in-scope starting point: EHR integration (SaaS EHR, read-only patient lookup), Scheduling API, and the usage pipeline that sends embeddings to Redwood-hosted inference.
- Decision roster: we heard that Tom is the technical lead, Evelyn will surface the procurement path, and Procurement/Security teams will own final acceptance.

What we’re attaching: a filled initial questionnaire template (orchid_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx) with placeholders based on today’s call and a simple network boundary diagram (orchid_network_boundary.png). Please review and flag anything that should be excluded or added.

Next proposed milestones: 
1) Orchid updates questionnaire with any corrections — target Tue 5/24.
2) Redwood schedules a kickoff call with your security team + procurement to walk the answers — propose Wed 5/25 10:00am PT.
3) Procurement shares contract path and any required PO/legal templates — by end of week.

Can you confirm the in-scope systems and whether PHI will be present in the data paths we discussed? Also please confirm who in Procurement should be looped on follow-ups (procurement@orchidhealth.com was mentioned).

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0133

Attachments: orchid_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx (Excel, 52 KB), orchid_network_boundary.png (image, 180 KB)

From: Evelyn Zhang <evelyn.zhang@orchidhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@orchidhealth.com>, procurement@orchidhealth.com, security-ops@orchidhealth.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: security questionnaire, in-scope systems & decision roster

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and for sending the questionnaire. A few clarifications from our side: 

- In-scope systems: the EHR integration (we use MediCloud), the scheduling system (SchedPro, via API), and the analytics pipeline that extracts de-identified metrics for reporting. The customer-facing chatbot will not be in scope for the initial review (we're treating that as a follow-on).
- PHI: yes — the EHR lookup will surface limited PHI (name, DOB, appointment times). We need encryption-at-rest and strict access logging for any PHI flows.
- Procurement contact: procurement@orchidhealth.com is correct (I copied them). Our procurement lead is Dana Patel — procurement@orchidhealth.com (she will take the contract lead).

We updated a few cells in your spreadsheet (see comments in the attached). Two asks from Security:
1) Can Redwood share a redacted example of the network boundary (if you have one) and the default retention settings for logs?
2) A brief note on whether your hosted inference option can be operated under our VPC/pinned model (we may need private deployment depending on final risk acceptance).

We can do the kickoff call on Wed 5/25 10:00am PT — Dana and our security lead (security-ops@orchidhealth.com) will join.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Director of Product Operations | Orchid Health
evelyn.zhang@orchidhealth.com

Forwarding Orchid's clarifications. Key takeaways for our pre-kickoff prep: 
- PHI will be present in the EHR lookup flow — need to confirm encryption and audit logging posture.
- They asked for a redacted network boundary / example and clarification on our VPC/private deployment options.
- Procurement lead is Dana (procurement@orchidhealth.com) — procurement will be on the Wed 5/25 call.

Actions for Redwood before 5/25 call: 
1) Priyom: prepare a 1-page redacted network boundary and a short note on default log retention/audit capabilities.
2) Ben: prepare a two-slide options summary for Hosted vs Private deployment (cost/latency/controls tradeoffs) and whether we can support a VPC pin.
3) Marissa: confirm scheduling and send a calendar invite with the Drive link and the questionnaire.

I’ll own the call agenda and will be in the meeting with the account.

-M

Thanks all — confirmed for Wed 5/25 10:00am PT. Quick notes ahead of kickoff: 

- Attached is a redacted boundary sketch (redacted_network_boundary.pdf) and a short bullet list on retention/audit defaults (see Drive link below). The redaction removes internal IPs and customer-specific hostnames.
- Host vs Private: Ben and I discussed — summary slides are attached to the shared Drive folder; short answer: Hosted API supports encryption-in-transit + per-tenant keying, but if Orchids wants full VPC isolation we can offer Redwood Private with a predictable reserved capacity quote. Ben, I’ll let you surface the numbers on the call.
- Regarding PHI: we suggested two mitigations to start the conversation — (a) tokenization/PII extraction at ingestion to minimize stored PHI, (b) strict RBAC and audit hooks for token access. We'll bring a short note and sample retention policy.

Drive (read-only link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AOrchidSharedDocLink
DocuSign placeholder: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/ORC-2027-042

See you on the call — Priyom
